note.text:
Grid lines are numbered lines drawn on a map to help us find places.
• Eastings are the lines going up and down. Their numbers are along the bottom and grow towards the east.
• Northings are the lines going across. Their numbers are up the side and grow towards the north.
A 4-figure grid reference names a square: first the easting of the line on the left of the square, then the northing of the line below it. Remember: “along the corridor, then up the stairs”.
A 6-figure grid reference names a point: imagine each side of the square cut into ten. Write the easting and the tenths across, then the northing and the tenths up. 253347 means easting 25 and 3 tenths, northing 34 and 7 tenths.

worked_example.problem: What is the four-figure grid reference of the clinic?
steps: Along the corridor: the line on the left of the clinic’s square is easting {e0 + 2}.
Up the stairs: the line below the square is northing {n0 + 1}.

cards.idea: Eastings are the grid lines going up and down; their numbers are along the bottom. Northings go across; their numbers are up the side.
example: Eastings grow as you go east (to the right). Northings grow as you go north (up).

right.text: Eastings are the lines going up and down the map.
Northings are the lines going across the map.
The easting numbers are written along the bottom of the map.

wrong.text: Eastings are the lines going across the map.
wrong.explain: Lines going across are northings. Eastings go up and down.

wrong.text: Northing numbers get bigger towards the south.
wrong.explain: Northing numbers get bigger towards the north.

wrong.text: Easting numbers get bigger towards the west.
wrong.explain: Easting numbers get bigger towards the east.

cards.idea: A four-figure grid reference names a square: the easting of the line on its left, then the northing of the line below it.
example: “Along the corridor, then up the stairs”: easting first, northing second.

cards.idea: To find a square from its grid reference, go along to the easting, then up to the northing: the square is to the right of and above that corner.
example: Square {grid4(e, n)}: along to easting {e}, up to northing {n}.

cards.idea: A six-figure grid reference names a point: easting and tenths across, then northing and tenths up.
example: {grid6(e, a, n, b)}: easting {e} and {a} tenths, northing {n} and {b} tenths.

check.prompt: In the grid reference {grid6(e, a, n, b)}, which part gives the easting and its tenths?

misconceptions.explain: That is the northing. The easting always comes first.
In a six-figure reference the easting has its tenths: three figures.
Split the six figures into two groups of three: easting first, northing second.

solution: Split {grid6(e, a, n, b)} into two groups of three figures.
The first group is the easting with its tenths: {answer}.

questions.prompt: Give the 4-figure grid reference of the {ps[0]}.

misconceptions.explain: You gave the northing first. Easting first: along the corridor, then up the stairs.
Use the easting on the LEFT of the square, not the right.
Use the northing BELOW the square, not above it.

solution: Along the corridor: the line on the left of the {ps[0]}’s square is easting {e0 + de}.
Up the stairs: the line below it is northing {n0 + dn}.

questions.prompt: Which place is in grid square {grid4(e0 + de, n0 + dn)}?

misconceptions.explain: Go along to easting {e0 + de} first, then up to northing {n0 + dn}. The square is to the right of and above that corner.

solution: Along to easting {e0 + de}, up to northing {n0 + dn}.
The square to the right of and above that corner holds the {answer}.

questions.prompt: Which is the right way to give a 4-figure grid reference?

right.text: The easting on the left of the square, then the northing below it.

wrong.text: The northing below the square, then the easting on its left.
wrong.explain: Easting first: along the corridor, then up the stairs.

wrong.text: The easting on the right of the square, then the northing above it.
wrong.explain: Use the lines on the left and below the square.

wrong.text: The number of the square counted from the top of the map.
wrong.explain: A grid reference uses the easting and northing numbers.

wrong.text: Any two numbers you can see near the place.
wrong.explain: Use the easting on the left of the square, then the northing below it.

questions.prompt: Give the 6-figure grid reference of the {ps[0]}.

misconceptions.explain: That gives the northing first. Easting and its tenths first, then northing and its tenths.
The tenths are mixed up: the first tenths are across (east), the second tenths are up (north).
Start from the easting on the left of the square, then add the tenths across.

solution: The {ps[0]} is right of easting {e0 + de} by {te} tenths of the square: {e0 + de}{te}.
It is above northing {n0 + dn} by {tn} tenths: {n0 + dn}{tn}.

questions.prompt: A pupil says the {ps[0]} is in square {grid4(n0 + dn, e0 + de)}. What mistake was made?
questions.correct: The northing was given before the easting.

distractors.text: The easting on the right of the square was used.
The northing above the square was used.
There is no mistake: the answer is right.

misconceptions.explain: Look again: the right answer is {grid4(e0 + de, n0 + dn)}. The same two numbers were used, in the wrong order.
The right answer is {grid4(e0 + de, n0 + dn)}: easting first, then northing.

solution: The {ps[0]}’s square has easting {e0 + de} and northing {n0 + dn}: {grid4(e0 + de, n0 + dn)}.
The same numbers were written the other way round. So: {answer}
